ops.title: Helper agents bake versioned install paths (Caskroom/keg) into plists — canonicalHelperProgram bypasses StableProgram staging
ops.description:
Found on yasyf-home during the synckit 0.36.2 cutover (2026-07-26, fleet-stabilization task fc39f885). The daemonkit-owned helper agent com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.reposync was materialized with `Program = /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/reposync/0.27.4/reposync` — the raw versioned Caskroom path — while the serve/reconcile agents on the same machine correctly get the staged `~/.daemonkit/bin/synckitd` via `dkservice.CanonicalExecutable()`.

Cause (read on-machine from the shipped synckit, pointing at the daemonkit helper-building path): `canonicalHelperProgram()` in daemon/service.go resolves the consumer executable via `exec.LookPath` + `EvalSymlinks` instead of the staging mechanism. EvalSymlinks through /opt/homebrew/bin/<name> lands on the versioned keg/Caskroom real path.

Consequence: every consumer brew upgrade moves the path and strands the helper plist pointing at a deleted directory — the exact stale-program class the v0.20.x StableProgram rework was built to end (see the 6-day unlinked-inode serve incident on the yasyf box). KeepAlive helpers make it worse: the running process survives on the unlinked inode until the next bootstrap cycle, which then fails.

Related but distinct: helper bootstrap also fails with launchd EIO on two machines (suspected LimitLoadToSessionType; causality test in flight on yasyf-home — separate record once the verdict lands). Fixing this staging bug does not fix that one.

ops.text: Helper agents' Program resolves through the same staged-canonical-executable mechanism as daemon agents (CanonicalExecutable/StableProgram), never a version-embedded install path
A regression test proves a helper plist survives the consumer binary's install path moving (brew upgrade simulation)
